About sources, numbering and grading

Wording, translation, numbering and grading differ between collections and editions, so check the original source before relying on any narration.

Text read inside QORA comes from an open Hadith dataset (fawazahmed0, served through jsDelivr). Gradings appear only when that dataset supplies them, and QORA adds none of its own.

These are important collections, not every Hadith ever recorded. A collection’s name is never proof that a report is authentic.

EDITORIAL STANDARDS

Trust is built into the process.

Source is not commentary

Canonical source text, translation, tafsir/commentary, Hadith, grading, scientific evidence, and AI explanation must be visually distinguished.

Rights are edition-specific

Free to view does not automatically mean permission to copy, host, modify, download, or sell. Record the exact license for each item.

Do not invent a citation

If evidence is missing, say: “I couldn’t verify this in the available sources.” AI output is not an authenticated religious ruling.

QORA is a study aid. For religious rulings, please consult qualified scholars.

NAMAZ · PRAYER TIMES

Prayer times

Choose your location to see accurate prayer times.

Next prayer — --

    Offline city list

    Today

      Next 7 days

      Choose a location to see the week.

      Accuracy & local masjid match

      Match your local masjid

      Enter the time your masjid or local timetable shows and QORA works out the minute offset for you. You can also type the offset directly (−60 to +60).

      Cross-check with an independent source

      Compares today’s times with the free AlAdhan calculator using the same coordinates and method. Only your coordinates, date and method are sent, and only when you press the button.

      Within about 10 km the calculated times differ by only a few seconds, so most differences between apps come from the method, the school (Asr) and rounding, not from distance. A local masjid may also follow its own fixed timetable, which is what the offsets are for.

      School of thought & method

      Leave elevation at 0 unless you have a clear, flat horizon (sea, open plain, a summit). The correction moves sunrise earlier and Maghrib later in the wrong direction for valleys and hill towns, where mountains hide the sun sooner. The detected elevation of a place is shown for information only and is never applied automatically.

      Alerts & alarms

      Web pages cannot ring while closed. For alarms that work with the app closed, add the calendar alarms: your phone calendar will notify you.

      Qibla & Hijri date

      Choose a location to see the Qibla direction.

      Custom coordinates

      For a spot that search cannot find, enter coordinates (for example copied from a map app).

      Prayer times are calculated on your device from the sun’s position, so they keep working offline. Searching for a place, naming a GPS fix and the optional cross-check contact free third-party services (Open-Meteo, BigDataCloud and AlAdhan) and send only the text you search for or the coordinates you choose. Methods differ between scholars and regions, so check against your local masjid or Islamic centre timetable and use the minute offsets if needed. Near the poles, high-latitude rules apply.

      Verification checklist

      HELP CENTRE

      Quick answers.

      Where is my data saved?

      Bookmarks, notes, progress and preferences are saved in this browser on your device. Sign in and turn on sync to keep them across devices.

      What is happening with Ask QORA?

      Ask QORA, our AI study assistant, is on and works without an account or key. Everything else (the Qur’an reader, Hadith, courses, tests and books) works as normal.

      Can I open a PDF?

      Yes. You can open a PDF from your device in the reading room. It stays on your device and is not uploaded.

      Can I publish a book?

      Authors can list a book, e-book, course or audiobook from Publish. Listings are reviewed before they appear in Books › Community.

      Something looks wrong. What should I do?

      Refresh the page first. If it persists, send us a short note with what you were doing and your device; we fix issues continuously.

      PRIVACY POLICY

      How QORA handles your data.

      Version 2026-10-31. QORA is designed, developed and operated by Zeeyan Rashid. This policy explains what is stored, what is shared, and the choices you have.

      At a glance

      No advertising cookies are set unless you accept them. Notes, bookmarks and reading progress stay on your device unless you turn on sync. We do not sell personal data. Location, microphone and notifications are used only if you allow them.

      Other services QORA contacts

      When a feature needs outside data, your browser contacts these services directly. Each one can see your IP address and the request itself, such as which surah or question you asked for. Their own privacy policies apply.

      • Qur’an text: api.alquran.cloud (verses and translations).
      • Recitation audio: cdn.islamic.network and audio.qurancdn.com.
      • Hadith: cdn.jsdelivr.net (Hadith data files from public projects) and hadeethenc.com. Opening a source link takes you to sunnah.com or the original site.
      • Adhan sounds: islamcan.com and archive.org.
      • Ask QORA AI: text.pollinations.ai by default, with no account. Your question is sent to that free service, so avoid personal details. If you add your own key, your question goes to the provider you choose (Google Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter or Hugging Face) instead, and the key is stored in this browser.
      • Accounts (optional): Supabase and Google, described above.

      Last updated: 5 November 2026.

      Who is responsible

      QORA is operated by Zeeyan Rashid, who decides how and why personal data described here is processed. Use the Contact page for privacy questions or requests.

      If you use QORA as a guest

      Bookmarks, notes, drafts, quiz progress, reading position, preferences and AI chat history are saved in your browser’s storage on your device. They are not sent to QORA unless you turn on sync. This storage is not encrypted and can be read by anyone using the same browser profile. Clearing browser data removes it. You can export or erase it in Settings.

      If you sign in with Google

      QORA uses Supabase to run accounts, with Google as the sign-in provider. From Google we receive your name, email address, profile-picture link and a Google account identifier. We never see your Google password. Supabase also records account and sign-in times and technical details such as IP address and browser, which are used to keep accounts secure. We store the date and version of the Terms and Privacy Policy you accepted on your account. Your browser keeps a sign-in token so you stay signed in until you sign out; “Sign out on all devices” ends every session.

      Optional online features

      Cross-device sync and publication applications send the data you choose (for example drafts, saved items, manuscripts and contact email) to QORA’s Supabase database, protected by row-level security so that other users cannot read your private records. Nothing is uploaded for sync until you switch it on.

      Cookies, ads and your consent

      QORA shows advertising through Google AdSense. No ad code is loaded and no advertising cookie is set until you choose to allow it. You can decline, accept, or choose settings, and you can change your mind at any time with Cookie settings. Your choice is remembered for 180 days and then asked again. Details are in the Cookie policy.

      Device permissions

      Location is requested only when you ask for prayer times or Qibla. It is saved on your device and sent to prayer-time and place-lookup services (AlAdhan, Open-Meteo, BigDataCloud) only when you use those features. Microphone is used for the recitation check; your browser’s speech recognition may process audio with its vendor (for example Google in Chrome), and QORA does not store recordings. Notifications are used for reminders you choose. Motion sensors are used for the Qibla compass. You can change any of these in your browser settings.

      Other services your browser may contact

      Content features load data from third-party sources such as AlQuran.cloud, the Islamic Network CDN, HadeethEnc, Crossref, OpenAlex, Europe PMC, Open Library and Wikipedia, which receive your IP address and the request. If you search for a place or use your location in Prayer times, Open-Meteo and BigDataCloud receive the text you searched or the coordinates you chose, and AlAdhan receives your coordinates if you press the cross-check button; each also receives your IP address. Supabase is hosted in Asia-Pacific (Singapore), so account data is processed outside your country. If you paste your own AI provider key, your questions go directly from your browser to that provider under its own terms. Do not enter passwords or sensitive personal details into AI tools.

      Legal bases (UK and EEA users)

      We rely on your consent for advertising cookies, optional device permissions and sync; on contract to run your account; and on our legitimate interests to keep the service secure and prevent abuse. You can withdraw consent at any time without affecting earlier processing.

      How long we keep data

      Data in your browser stays until you clear it. Account and synced data stay until you delete your account or ask us to delete it. Your cookie choice is stored for 180 days. Sign-in and security logs are kept by Supabase according to its own retention rules.

      Your choices and rights

      Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, delete or export your data, to object to or restrict processing, to withdraw consent, and to complain to your data-protection authority. Use Settings to export or erase local data and the Contact page for account requests. You can manage ad personalisation at adssettings.google.com.

      Children

      QORA is for a general audience and is not directed at children under 13 (or the age set by local law). We do not knowingly collect personal data from children. If you believe a child has created an account, contact us and we will delete it.

      Security

      QORA is served over HTTPS and uses a strict Content Security Policy, which limits which scripts can run. Accounts use row-level security. No system is perfectly secure; keep your Google account protected and do not store sensitive information in notes or AI chats.

      Changes

      We update this policy when features or laws change. The version date is shown at the top. If a change affects advertising or consent, we will ask for your choice again.

      COOKIE POLICY

      Cookies and similar storage.

      Version 2026-10-31. This page lists what QORA stores in your browser and how you stay in control.

      What this means

      Cookies are small files a website saves in your browser. QORA mostly uses your browser’s local storage instead, which works in a similar way. Both are covered here.

      What QORA stores

      TypeWhatPurposeHow longConsent needed?
      Essentialqora.consent.v1Remembers your cookie choice180 daysNo
      EssentialSettings, reading position, bookmarks, notes, drafts, quiz progress, AI chats (browser storage, keys starting qora)Features you useUntil you clear themNo

      AdvertisingGoogle AdSense cookies such as __gads, __gpi, __eoi, FCNEC, plus cookies on Google domainsShow and measure adsSet by Google, typically up to 13 monthsYes: only after you accept

      Advertising and your choice

      QORA uses Google AdSense. Until you accept, QORA does not load Google’s ad code and sets no advertising cookies. If you decline, nothing is loaded. If you accept, Google and its partners may set cookies to show and measure ads under Google’s own policies. Your choice lasts 180 days, and you can change it at any time. Withdrawing consent removes the ad cookies QORA can reach and reloads the page without ads.

      More controls

      You can also delete cookies and site data in your browser settings. Manage Google ad personalisation at adssettings.google.com. Learn how Google uses data from partner sites at policies.google.com. Industry opt-out tools: optout.aboutads.info and youronlinechoices.eu.

      Questions

      See the Privacy policy for how your data is handled, or use the Contact page.

      QORA may contain incomplete records. It must not be used as an authoritative religious source, legal, medical or scientific opinion, or as proof that any item is licensed for redistribution.

      QORA links to and loads content from third parties. We do not control them and are not responsible for their content or practices.

      Availability

      QORA is provided as is. Much of your data is stored only in your browser, and there is no guarantee of backup, uninterrupted availability, or any particular publishing outcome. Export important work from Settings.

      Warranties and liability

      To the extent allowed by law, QORA is provided without warranties of any kind, and the operator is not liable for indirect or consequential loss arising from your use of QORA. Nothing in these terms limits rights you have under law that cannot be excluded.
